item.content:encoded: I could see the first one being right, but this isn't even particularly close to "Let her finish her meal". That'd be something like cenam peragat (I say something like because that's a simplified version which implies "let" and the meal being hers instead of outright stating it). Vescor is the verb meaning "to eat".

item.content:encoded: It probably means (I say probably because there's no context for the subjunctive verb, meaning that it's most likely, but not surely hortatory) "I finish let her eat." On the upside for the poorly done Latin title, ecce perago means "Behold I finish," so it's fitting that this one doesn't make sense either.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Egh. Ecce Perago really didn't need re-imagining, even if part two was just "Let's make every SSAA into an O5". It's still a solid tale, the kills in it are fairly creative, and it has a pretty good payoff.

This whole thing reads like a half-hearted gore fic, in the vein of Cupcakes or Dipper goes to Taco Bell (Do not look either of those up, for the love of god), but less willing to go whole hog with the details. I feel like this wants to be Saw meets the X-Files episode "Our Town"1, but it doesn't hit the shock value of the former nor the subtle horror of the latter. It just kind of… is.

I had no real reaction from it, so no vote.

Footnotes
1. For those of you not familiar with it, it's about a town of cannibals who discovered they can gain immortality by eating human flesh. They're pretty much wiped out by an outbreak of Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease after eating an infected human brain.
